# Green Expo Journeys

> Private, tailor-made tours of Sri Lanka with your own car and driver-guide. Run by Green Expo (S N S Ceylon Exports (Pvt) Ltd), a Sri Lankan exporter of coconut products, spices and tea based in Dankotuwa since 2012. Tours visit 28 places across the island, including the tea estates, spice gardens and coconut country the company sources from.

- Contact: info@greenexpolk.com, +94 71 148 6677 (phone and WhatsApp)
- Office: 85 Katukenda East, Dankotuwa, Sri Lanka
- All trips are private; enquiries are answered within a day with a plan and a price; no booking fee
- Airport pick-up at Bandaranaike International Airport (Katunayake)

## Places by region

### North-west coast
- Katunayake: The international airport. We meet you at arrivals. (20 min to Negombo)
- Negombo: Dawn fish market, then a boat through the lagoon’s mangroves. (20 min from the airport)
- Dankotuwa: Walk a coconut estate and have lunch with us. (40 min from Negombo)
- Chilaw: An ancient Shiva temple and a wetland full of pelicans and storks. (45 min from Dankotuwa)
- Puttalam: A quiet lagoon town, and the way into Wilpattu National Park. (1 h from Chilaw)
- Kalpitiya: Spinner dolphins November to April, kitesurfing May to October. (1 h from Puttalam)

### Far north
- Jaffna: Temples, an old Dutch fort, crab curry and the ferry to Delft Island. (7 h by train from Colombo)
- Point Pedro: The island’s northernmost point: fishing boats, a lighthouse and sand dunes. (45 min from Jaffna)

### Cultural Triangle
- Anuradhapura: Giant white stupas and a sacred Bo tree planted over 2,000 years ago. (3.5 h from Jaffna)
- Sigiriya: The 5th-century citadel. Climb it at first light. (2 h from Anuradhapura)
- Polonnaruwa: Royal ruins by a vast lake, and the rock-cut Buddhas of Gal Vihara. (1 h from Sigiriya)

### East coast
- Trincomalee: Clifftop Koneswaram, snorkelling at Pigeon Island and whales in season. (2 h from Polonnaruwa)
- Batticaloa: A lagoon town with a Dutch fort, a lighthouse and its famous “singing fish”. (3 h from Trincomalee)
- Arugam Bay: A laid-back surf beach. The point break is best May to September. (3 h from Batticaloa)

### Deep south
- Yala: Dawn safaris in leopard country. Closed September to mid October. (2.5 h from Arugam Bay)
- Kataragama: Sacred to Buddhists, Hindus and Muslims. Join the evening puja. (30 min from Yala)
- Tangalle: Long, empty bays, with turtles nesting at nearby Rekawa. (1.5 h from Kataragama)
- Dikwella: Hiriketiya’s horseshoe surf cove and a giant seated Buddha. (30 min from Tangalle)
- Dondra Head: The island’s southernmost point and its tallest lighthouse. (20 min from Dikwella)
- Mirissa: Blue whales November to April, then the beach. (15 min from Dondra Head)
- Galle: Sunset on the 17th-century ramparts. (45 min from Mirissa)

### Hill country
- Ratnapura: The city of gems, with waterfalls and Sinharaja rainforest within reach. (2.5 h from Galle)
- Sri Pada: Climb through the night for sunrise at the summit, December to May. (Trails from Ratnapura or Hatton)
- Nuwara Eliya: Stay on a tea estate and pluck with the morning shift. (2 h from Hatton)
- Bandarawela: A quiet tea town with cool air and views down to the plains. (1.5 h from Nuwara Eliya)
- Ella: The hill-country train and the Nine Arch Bridge. (30 min from Bandarawela)
- Kandy: Evening puja at the Temple of the Tooth, then the lake. (4 h from Ella)
- Matale: Cinnamon, cardamom, nutmeg and pepper, grown side by side. (40 min from Kandy)

## Itineraries

- The Classic Loop (12 days): Rock fortress, tea country, leopards and the south coast. Best: December to April.
- Lagoons and Dolphins (4 days): Negombo, our coconut estate, wetlands and Kalpitiya’s dolphins. Best: Dolphins Nov–Apr, kitesurfing May–Oct.
- Jaffna and the East (6 days): Jaffna, Delft Island and the beaches of Trincomalee. Best: February to September.
- Tea Country by Train (5 days): Kandy to Ella by train, with two nights on a tea estate. Best: January to April.
- Leopards and the South (6 days): Yala safaris, whales at Mirissa and Galle Fort. Best: December to April.
- A Day with Us (1 day): Fish market, lagoon and lunch at our estate. Best: All year.

## When to go (summary)

- When is the best time to visit Sri Lanka? It depends on the coast. December to April is best for the west and south coasts and the hill country. April to September is best for the east coast and the north. Somewhere on the island is usually dry in every month.
- When is whale watching in Sri Lanka? Off Mirissa on the south coast, roughly November to April. Off Trincomalee on the east coast, roughly March to August.
- When can you climb Sri Pada (Adam’s Peak)? The pilgrim season runs from about December to May, when the path is lit at night and the weather is clearest.
- Is Yala National Park open all year? No. Yala usually closes in September and the first half of October.
